query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: For single-phase, body-centered-cubic (BCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that do not contain the canonical Nb–Ta matrix, the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) is governed primarily by the average valence-electron concentration (VEC). Tc reaches a maximum when the alloy’s VEC is near 4.7 ± 0.1 e⁄atom; moving the VEC away from this optimum on either side lowers Tc because the electronic density of states at the Fermi level (N(EF)) decreases, weakening electron-phonon coupling.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Hf–Zr–Ti–V–Cr high-entropy alloy (single-phase BCC, VEC ≈ 4.4 e⁄atom, reported Tc ≈ 7.5 K).
generation.intervention: Substitute 10 at % of Cr with Ni (yielding nominal composition Hf19Zr19Ti19V19Cr9Ni15, overall VEC ≈ 4.6 e⁄atom, no other processing changes).
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure; zero magnetic field; temperature range 2 K – 15 K; samples annealed 24 h at 1000 °C followed by water quench to preserve single-phase BCC solid solution.
generation.structural_mediator: Change in electronic density of states at the Fermi level (N(EF)) arising from the shifted VEC while the BCC lattice parameter and disorder remain essentially unchanged.
generation.mechanism: Moving the average VEC toward 4.7 e⁄atom raises N(EF), strengthening electron-phonon coupling (λ) in the McMillan framework. Stronger λ increases the pairing interaction responsible for superconductivity, thereby raising Tc. Excess deviation of VEC in either direction lowers N(EF) and λ, suppressing Tc.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy, the Ni-substituted sample (VEC ≈ 4.6) will show (i) an increase in Tc by ≃ 1 K (to ~8.5–9 K), (ii) a larger specific-heat jump at Tc, and (iii) an ~10–20 % higher Sommerfeld coefficient γ extracted from low-temperature heat-capacity fits, indicating higher N(EF).
generation.baseline: Tc ≈ 7.5 K, ΔC⁄γTc ≈ 1.3, and γ ≈ 4 mJ mol⁻¹ K⁻² for the equiatomic Hf–Zr–Ti–V–Cr alloy.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis applies only to (1) chemically disordered, single-phase BCC HEAs composed of early transition metals plus ≤20 at % late, non-magnetic transition metals, (2) VEC range 4.0–6.0 e⁄atom, (3) absence of long-range magnetic order. Outside these ranges other factors (magnetism, multi-phase segregation, strong electron correlations) dominate and prediction may fail.
generation.uncertainty: No direct experimental data yet exist for the proposed composition; magnitude of Tc change is estimated from trends in related BCC HEAs, so numerical shift (≈1 K) is uncertain to ±0.5 K.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three alloys: (A) baseline equiatomic Hf–Zr–Ti–V–Cr (VEC ≈ 4.4), (B) Ni-modified alloy described above (VEC ≈ 4.6), and (C) an alloy with added Cu instead of Ni to raise VEC to ≈ 4.8. Confirm single-phase BCC by X-ray diffraction and STEM-EDS. Measure resistivity and specific heat from 2 K to 15 K under zero field.
measurements: Onset and midpoint Tc from resistivity and magnetization
Sommerfeld coefficient γ from C/T versus T² below 3 K
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Tc does not increase for alloy B relative to A, or if alloy C (VEC ≈ 4.8) shows an equal or higher Tc than alloy B, or if γ fails to follow Tc (i.e., N(EF) does not peak near VEC ≈ 4.7), the hypothesis is falsified.
